introduction: A high-end retail facade combined folded silver metal backing, clear prismatic facing and integrated lighting around large framed openings. Workshop images show the steel support frame, the folded backing and the corner mock-up as separate assemblies. On the lighting test bay, white and warm settings reveal how the repeated folds catch light. Installed views show how the illuminated treatment meets window heads, jambs and the exterior corner.

sections.title: An illuminated panel system for a framed retail elevation
paragraphs: The visible system brings the folded backing, prismatic outer elements and lights together within a framed panel. The architectural metalwork also defines the edges where these panels meet openings, corner returns and darker vertical trims.

sections.title: Keep the facade pattern continuous across changing conditions
paragraphs: The facade is read by reflected and transmitted light. Regular fold spacing matters across the face, but breaks in the rhythm become most visible where two modules meet an opening or turn a corner.

points.title: Repeated fold geometry
points.text: Small changes in fold pitch show as irregular bands of light when neighboring pieces are seen together.

points.title: Optical layer and light placement
points.text: Use a mock-up to review the distance between the light source, reflective backing and prismatic elements. The relationship changes how individual highlights combine across the face.

points.title: Perimeter and corner returns
points.text: The steel frame, finished trim and facing must meet in the same piece of geometry so the illuminated pattern can reach the edges cleanly.

sections.title: Folded backing panels and steel frames for the openings
paragraphs: The fabrication photographs show silver profiles grouped by their folded section. On the bench, timber bars and clamps hold the repeated folds in line across a panel.

The steel frames were laid out in the workshop and stood upright to bring the window openings and head rails into alignment. Detail views show the bolted brackets and the transition between the frame and finished trim.

sections.title: Dry-fit the elevation and compare light in the same test bay
paragraphs: The upright workshop trial brought the folded panels, opening frames and corner trims together at full height. Close-ups show how the trim ends and dark reveals meet at an inside corner.
In the lighting trial, the same backing geometry was photographed with white and warm light at the edges. A separate two-sided mock-up shows the clear faceted facing where it turns around a corner.

sections.title: Illuminated exterior corners and display surrounds
paragraphs: The dusk exterior shows the vertical prismatic pattern around successive display windows and across two adjoining elevations. The darker steel-and-metal framing between the illuminated sections makes the rhythm of the bays legible at building scale.
A separate display edge close-up shows the detail at a dark jamb. These installed views give designers both the approach distance and a close reference for how a facing meets a surrounding profile.

gallery.caption: The vertical joint separates the illuminated facing from the darker frame at the edge of the display opening.

sections.title: Scope an illuminated facade mock-up around a real junction
paragraphs: Include a straight bay, one opening edge and a return in the design brief so the lighting review covers the junctions that visitors will see.

points.title: Drawings and services
points.text: Submit CAD or PDF elevations with head, jamb and corner sections. Show allowable build-up, driver and cable locations, drainage requirements, and maintenance access.

points.title: Sample and viewing conditions
points.text: Define the fold profile, facing finish, lighting target and intended viewing distance. Review the same mock-up under each intended lighting setting and ambient condition.

points.title: Access and movement
points.text: Confirm module handling dimensions, the erection route, access to connections and movement joints at neighboring construction.

conclusion: Folded backing and prismatic facing can build a consistent vertical rhythm across a lit flagship elevation. The frame, light placement and facing edges need to be resolved as a single detail around doors, windows and corners. Send your CAD or PDF elevations, sections and lighting intent to define a workshop mock-up around the most visible junction.
